title: Rethinking Economic Measurement Using Statistical Ensembles
content: Statistical ensembles are a new and unfamiliar concept in economics. Many of the longstanding problems in economics such as the Allais paradox and being unable to formally aggregate micro-principles into macro-observations are readily resolved through the analytical framework of ensembles. We apply the canonical ensemble to three distinct economic spheres. We examine choice under uncertainty and find that the Allais paradox disappears; having acted as a barrier to exploring human choice for over a seventy-years by masking actual choice heuristics. We connect the canonical ensemble to the idea of a Cobb—Douglas production function and examine income distributions in the United States over a 24-year period and find that we can predict with surprising accuracy economic behavior just using the income distribution and the total exergy input into the economy. Finally, we examine the ideas of equality of outcome versus equality of opportunity. We show how equality of outcome can be formally considered in economics and how its achievement leads to a necessary collapse in economic activity. This is by no means an exhaustive exposition of Statistical Economics. It is merely a highlight of various areas that economists have been unable to resolve within their current analytical frameworks.
